source_note: Catalog title '2509.05913v3' and primary_domain 'other' are catalog placeholders. True source: Rahman, Karim, Raiaan, Shermin, Islam, Hussain, Azam, 'A Fine-Grained Attention and Geometric Correspondence Model for Musculoskeletal Risk Classification in Athletes Using Multimodal Visual and Skeletal Features' (ViSK-GAT), arXiv:2509.05913v3 [cs.CV], 23 pages, clean born-digital text. Tier-B queue row but a full equation-rich research paper; extracted under true domain cs/physiology (sports ergonomics / musculoskeletal risk). Equations 1-16 transcribed as labeled LaTeX from the printed text; vector-arrow and norm glyphs in the PDF rendered as Unicode, reconstructed in standard notation. No sportsbook content. Dataset/code at github.com/mak-raiaan/MusDis-Sports_Dataset (research-use request).

primitives.name: MediaPipe 33-landmark normalized keypoint set
primitives.verbatim_quote: This framework outputs 33 anatomical keypoints corresponding to major joints and body segments.
assumptions: Monocular 2D image input; coordinates normalized to image frame.
Pretrained MediaPipe model used as a fixed, reproducible keypoint extractor.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks under severe self-occlusion, non-frontal viewpoints, and motion blur where 2D landmarks become unreliable; depth is unobservable from a single frame.

layer2.mapping: The normalized keypoint set IS the GSE/GSI body-state observation kernel: a fixed-dimensional, visibility-weighted pose vector that grounds every downstream physical-reasoning operator in measurable joint geometry rather than opaque pixels.
layer2.telemetry: 33 landmarks x (x,y,v); visibility confidence v_i in [0,1]; MediaPipe pretrained extractor.

primitives.name: Visibility-confidence landmark gating
primitives.verbatim_quote: The remaining coordinates were scaled to the original image dimensions, forming the 2D skeletal matrix
assumptions: A landmark with visibility below 0.5 is treated as unreliable and excluded.
Retained normalized coordinates are rescaled to original image pixel dimensions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Threshold is a hard cutoff: a landmark at v=0.49 is discarded while v=0.51 is kept, so borderline-confidence joints introduce discontinuous skeleton topology.

layer2.mapping: Visibility gating IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSE observation-quality veto: low-confidence telemetry is dropped before it can corrupt a physical estimate, mirroring the doctrine that an uncertain sensor reading must not silently enter a sovereign primitive.
layer2.telemetry: v_i < 0.5 hard threshold; rescale to image pixels; 33x2 skeletal matrix.

primitives.name: Cosine-law joint angle from keypoint triplets
primitives.verbatim_quote: First, we calculated the joint angles using the cosine law.
assumptions: Three non-collinear keypoints define a joint angle at the middle point B.
Angles computed in the 2D image plane, not 3D anatomical space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity when ||BA|| or ||BC|| -> 0 (coincident keypoints) gives division by zero; near-collinear triplets make the angle ill-conditioned and noise-sensitive.

layer2.mapping: The cosine-law joint angle IS the GSI bioenergetic joint-stress primitive: a coordinate-invariant scalar measuring limb flexion that feeds ergonomic load estimation, exactly the kind of dimensioned, breakdown-aware operator the Foundry requires.
layer2.telemetry: theta in radians; dot product over Euclidean norms; 2D triplet geometry.

primitives.name: Slope-based trunk vertical inclination with epsilon guard
primitives.verbatim_quote: Second, vertical inclination angles were computed to assess postural deviations like trunk or neck flexion.

symbol_and_unit_ledger.epsilon: small constant preventing division by zero [pixels]

assumptions: Trunk orientation approximated by the shoulder-hip midpoint segment.
epsilon added to numerator to avoid a zero/zero form in near-vertical postures.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks when |y_shoulder - y_hip| -> 0 (horizontal trunk) where the inclination diverges; epsilon regularizes the near-vertical case but not the horizontal singularity.

layer2.mapping: Trunk inclination IS a GSI postural-load kernel: the epsilon-guarded arctangent is a worked example of the singularity-regime discipline the Foundry mandates, encoding both the measurable quantity and its exact breakdown boundary.
layer2.telemetry: theta in radians; epsilon guard; shoulder-hip midpoint segment.

primitives.name: REBA Group A aggregation (trunk, neck, legs)
primitives.verbatim_quote: the trunk, neck, and leg scores were aggregated to derive the Group A score

symbol_and_unit_ledger.s_neck,s_trunk,s_leg: region posture scores from joint-angle thresholds [ordinal integers]

assumptions: Region scores assigned by angle thresholds inspired by REBA guidelines.
Group A combines trunk, neck, and leg via the published lookup table.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Lookup-table aggregation is discrete and non-differentiable; small angle errors near a threshold boundary flip the ordinal region score.

layer2.mapping: Group A aggregation IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSI regional-load composition: discrete ergonomic lookup tables compose lower-body and axial posture scores into a single ordinal risk, a transparent alternative to a learned black-box mapping.
layer2.telemetry: Group A lookup table; trunk/neck/leg ordinal scores; REBA Hignett-McAtamney protocol.

primitives.name: REBA Group B aggregation (upper arm, lower arm, wrist)
primitives.verbatim_quote: the upper arm, lower arm, and wrist scores were combined to obtain the Group B score

symbol_and_unit_ledger.s_upper,s_lower,s_wrist: upper-arm, lower-arm, wrist posture scores [ordinal integers]

assumptions: Upper-limb region scores assigned from estimated joint angles.
Group B combines upper arm, lower arm, and wrist via the published lookup table.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Discrete table composition; wrist and forearm angle estimation noise propagates into the ordinal Group B score near threshold boundaries.

layer2.mapping: Group B aggregation IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSI upper-limb load composition, pairing with Group A so that the full-body risk is assembled from anatomically grounded regional scores rather than a monolithic classifier.
layer2.telemetry: Group B lookup table; upper-arm/lower-arm/wrist ordinal scores.

primitives.name: REBA Group C final risk matrix and 8-class labeling
primitives.verbatim_quote: These two group scores were subsequently mapped to a final REBA risk level through a predefined matrix

symbol_and_unit_ledger.g_A,g_B: Group A and Group B scores [ordinal integers]

assumptions: Group C matrix maps the (g_A, g_B) pair to a final REBA score.
Final scores partitioned into 8 classes; higher class number indicates riskier posture.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The model learns to predict the output of a fixed rule-based function, not an unconstrained mapping; class boundaries inherit the discreteness of the REBA tables.

layer2.mapping: The Group C matrix IS the GSI ordinal-risk labeling kernel: a deterministic, interpretable function from regional posture scores to a ranked risk class, which is precisely the sovereign, auditable target the Foundry prefers over opaque labels.
layer2.telemetry: Group C lookup matrix; 8 ordinal classes; class >=4 riskier; rule-based target.

primitives.name: Load and activity modifiers fixed to zero (single-frame scope)
primitives.verbatim_quote: As our dataset consists of single-frame images without dynamic tasks or load handling, we fixed both the load and activity modifiers to zero.

symbol_and_unit_ledger.0_load: external-load modifier fixed to zero [ordinal integer]
symbol_and_unit_ledger.0_activity: repetitive-activity modifier fixed to zero [ordinal integer]

assumptions: Single-frame static images carry no observable external load or repetition.
Load and activity modifiers, part of full REBA, are set to zero by design.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks the moment risk is load-driven or repetition-driven rather than postural: the score systematically under-risks tasks where external load or repeated motion dominates.

layer2.mapping: Zeroed modifiers IS a DERIVED KERNEL exposing GSE scope-of-observability veto: a risk model must declare which causal modifiers it cannot observe and set them to a documented constant rather than hallucinate them, exactly the epistemic separation the Foundry enforces.
layer2.telemetry: load=0, activity=0; single-frame static scope; full REBA modifiers omitted.

primitives.name: 2D REBA approximation preserving relative joint-stress ranking
primitives.verbatim_quote: we employed a 2D approximation for broader applicability in conventional available image data that preserves the relative ranking of joint stresses.
assumptions: 2D angular displacements used in place of 3D angular measurements.
Approximation preserves relative ranking of joint stresses, not absolute 3D angles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: The 2D approximation IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSI measurement-fidelity tradeoff: a documented projection that sacrifices absolute 3D accuracy for monocular accessibility while preserving the ordinal ranking that decision-making actually consumes.
layer2.telemetry: 2D vs 3D REBA; relative ranking preserved; monocular accessibility tradeoff.

primitives.name: Automatic-label reliability via ICC and manual sanity check
primitives.verbatim_quote: We also processed the samples under slightly varied viewing scales and compared them using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC = 0.84).

symbol_and_unit_ledger.ICC: intraclass correlation coefficient of label stability across viewing scales [dimensionless, 0-1]

assumptions: Labeling stability assessed by re-processing samples under varied viewing scales.
Manual sanity check on a random 500-image subset; visibility filter and geometry-consistency checks applied.
primitives.breakdown_regime: ICC 0.84 indicates good but not perfect stability; labels remain a 2D-estimation tolerance, not ground-truth 3D ergonomic assessment.

layer2.mapping: ICC label-stability auditing IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSE provenance-quality gate: automatically derived labels must carry a measured reliability statistic and a human sanity-check sample before they are allowed to supervise a sovereign model.
layer2.telemetry: ICC=0.84; 500-image manual sanity check; visibility + geometry-consistency filters.

primitives.name: MusDis-Sports multimodal dataset composition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our MusDis-Sports dataset comprises 8989 annotated samples, each consisting of an image of a human subject in a sports-related posture
assumptions: 8989 image + 2D-skeleton + REBA-class triples compiled from public sports datasets.
Sources: Sports-1M, Sports Classification, Sports Image Classification, Cricket Shot; full-body visible frames only.
primitives.breakdown_regime: no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: MusDis-Sports IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSI multimodal-corpus construction: heterogeneous public image sources unified under a single ergonomic labeling protocol, the same provenance-first corpus assembly the Foundry applies to its PDF swarm.
layer2.telemetry: 8989 samples; 8 REBA classes; 4 public source datasets; full-body visibility filter.

primitives.name: Learnable linear pose-token embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: which was then projected to a higher-dimensional space using a learnable linear transformation
primitives.latex: F_{pose}^{emb} = P\,W_e + b_e,\quad W_e\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times d},\ b_e\in\mathbb{R}^{d}

symbol_and_unit_ledger.P: flattened skeleton joint tokens [N x 2, normalized coords]
symbol_and_unit_ledger.W_e: learned pose-embedding weight matrix [2 x d]

assumptions: Skeleton flattened into a sequence of 2D joint tokens before projection.
A lightweight Transformer then models long-range joint correlations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Linear projection alone cannot capture joint-angle nonlinearities; the subsequent self-attention block is required for higher-order posture dependencies.

layer2.mapping: The pose-token embedding IS the GSE structured-to-latent observation kernel: raw coordinate telemetry is lifted into a shared latent space where attention can reason over joint relationships, the canonical first step of any sovereign physical-reasoning stack.
layer2.telemetry: W_e in R^{2xd}; P in R^{Nx2}; latent dim d; followed by Transformer self-attention.

primitives.name: Fine-Grained Attention Module intra-modal refinement before fusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our goal was to let each image patch attend to others within the same modality and enhance discriminative posture cues before engaging in cross-modal fusion.
assumptions: Image tokens refined by multi-head self-attention (8 heads) within the image modality first.
Two lightweight Transformer blocks (128->512->128 FFN) follow the initial attention layer.
primitives.breakdown_regime: no_equation_domain

layer2.mapping: FGAM IS the GSE intra-modal refinement kernel: refining a modality's own representation before cross-modal alignment ensures the fusion operates on posture-cue-aware features rather than diffuse general-purpose activations, a structural prerequisite the Foundry maps onto its layered reasoning pipeline.
layer2.telemetry: 8 attention heads; 2 lightweight Transformer blocks; FFN 128->512->128; pre-fusion refinement.

primitives.name: FGAM residual addition and layer normalization
primitives.verbatim_quote: To preserve the original representation, we added a residual connection followed by a layer normalization operation.
assumptions: Residual addition preserves the original representation across refinement.
Layer normalization stabilizes the refined token distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Residual+norm guards against gradient vanishing but does not fix mis-aligned posture cues; depth beyond two blocks yields no gain (ablation A4).

layer2.mapping: The residual+LayerNorm refinement IS the GSE stability-preserving update kernel: identity-preserving residual structure plus normalization is the same conservation-minded design the Foundry requires so that refinement never destroys the sovereign signal it refines.
layer2.telemetry: F3 in R^{256x128}; FFN 128->512->128; LayerNorm residual.

primitives.name: MGCM asymmetric cross-attention (image query, pose key/value)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Image tokens serve as queries while coordinate tokens serve as keys and values, grounding the visual representation in the geometric structure of the body.

symbol_and_unit_ledger.F'_img: projected image tokens serving as queries [256 x d, d=256]
symbol_and_unit_ledger.F'_pose: projected coordinate tokens serving as keys and values [33 x d]

assumptions: Asymmetric Q/K/V assignment motivated by biomechanics: joint positions guide selection of visual features.
Both modalities projected into a common latent space before cross-attention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Direct cross-attention without prior alignment produces suboptimal correspondences because visual texture and geometric coordinates occupy different representational spaces.

layer2.mapping: Asymmetric geometric cross-attention IS the GSE cross-layer correspondence kernel: grounding appearance queries in skeletal geometry is the exact isomorphism of grounding a market/visual prior in a sovereign physical state, the Foundry's central fusion pattern.
layer2.telemetry: Q=F'_img (256xd), K=V=F'_pose (33xd), d=256; biomechanically motivated asymmetry.

primitives.name: MGCM fused representation and fusion head
primitives.verbatim_quote: To capture higher-order cross-modal interactions and enrich geometric understanding
assumptions: Fused representation processed by 2 stacked Transformer layers (4 heads, FFN expanded to 4d).
Fusion head = linear + LayerNorm + GELU producing the 512-dim joint embedding.
primitives.breakdown_regime: A third Transformer layer overfits the compact 512-dim fused representation (ablation B5); concatenation alone cannot recover geometric alignment (B1, -2.82% F1).

layer2.mapping: The fusion head IS the GSE multimodal-decision embedding kernel: a fixed-dimensional joint representation assembled by geometric alignment and refined by attention, the sovereign fused state from which a calibrated decision head reads.
layer2.telemetry: F_corr in R^512; 2 Transformer layers, 4 heads, FFN 4d; linear+LayerNorm+GELU head.

primitives.name: Classification accuracy metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: To assess the performance of the proposed multimodal posture risk classification model, we employed a comprehensive set of evaluation metrics
assumptions: Accuracy computed over the confusion matrix of the 8-class task.
Reported alongside chance-adjusted metrics because accuracy alone can mislead under imbalance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Accuracy is misleading under class imbalance; the authors therefore also report Cohen's Kappa and MCC.

layer2.mapping: Accuracy IS the GSE base-rate scoring kernel, but the Foundry inherits the paper's own caveat: a raw hit-rate must be paired with chance-adjusted metrics before it can certify a decision layer.
layer2.telemetry: TP/TN/FP/FN counts; 8-class confusion matrix; imbalance caveat.

primitives.name: Precision metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: We note that precision for class 2 is the lowest overall (88.46%)
assumptions: Precision defined per class from the confusion matrix.
Class 2 precision lowest overall (88.46%), reflecting narrow low-to-moderate risk thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undefined when TP+FP=0 (no positive predictions); low precision in boundary classes signals false-alarm concentration.

layer2.mapping: Precision IS the GSE false-alarm veto kernel: the cost of crying wolf on a risk class is exactly the precision denominator the Foundry weighs before allowing an alert to fire.
layer2.telemetry: TP/(TP+FP); class 2 lowest 88.46%; false-alarm concentration.

primitives.name: Recall (sensitivity) metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: and recall for class 4 is the lowest (87.70%)
assumptions: Recall defined per class from the confusion matrix.
Class 4 recall lowest (87.70%), the weakest overall class.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undefined when TP+FN=0; low recall in high-risk classes is the critical failure mode for a safety system.

layer2.mapping: Recall IS the GSE miss-detection veto kernel: for high-risk postures the cost of a false negative dominates, so recall on the riskiest classes is the governing safety metric.
layer2.telemetry: TP/(TP+FN); class 4 lowest 87.70%; high-risk miss-detection cost.

primitives.name: F1-score harmonic mean of precision and recall
primitives.verbatim_quote: The model demonstrates consistently strong classification ability across all REBA classes, with F1-scores ranging from 88% to 99%.
assumptions: F1 computed per class; overall F1 93.85%.
Per-class F1 ranges 88% to 99% across the 8 REBA classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Harmonic mean penalizes imbalance between precision and recall; undefined when both are zero.

layer2.mapping: F1 IS the GSE balanced-decision score kernel: the harmonic mean forces a decision layer to be simultaneously precise and sensitive, the same dual requirement the Foundry places on any certified pick or risk alert.
layer2.telemetry: 2PR/(P+R); overall 93.85%; per-class 88-99%.

primitives.name: Matthews Correlation Coefficient
primitives.verbatim_quote: MCC measures classification quality across all confusion matrix categories
assumptions: MCC uses all four confusion-matrix categories, robust to class imbalance.
Reported MCC 0.93 for the full model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Denominator zero when any marginal count is zero (degenerate single-class prediction); range -1 (total disagreement) to +1 (perfect).

layer2.mapping: MCC IS the GSE imbalance-robust certification kernel: a single chance-aware correlation over the full confusion matrix is the Foundry's preferred summary when class distributions are skewed, exactly as the paper adopts it.
layer2.telemetry: MCC in [-1,+1]; reported 0.93; all four confusion categories.

primitives.name: Cohen's Kappa chance-adjusted agreement
primitives.verbatim_quote: quantifies agreement between predicted and true labels, adjusted for chance
assumptions: Unweighted Cohen's Kappa used; kappa=1 perfect, kappa=0 random agreement.
Reported kappa 0.93 for the full model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undefined when p_e=1 (perfect chance agreement); kappa can be low despite high accuracy under strong imbalance.

layer2.mapping: Cohen's Kappa IS the GSE chance-adjusted agreement kernel: subtracting expected chance agreement is the Foundry's guard against celebrating a hit-rate that a coin-flip baseline would also achieve.
layer2.telemetry: (p_o-p_e)/(1-p_e); reported 0.93; kappa=0 random baseline.

primitives.name: RMSE of predicted probability vector vs one-hot truth
primitives.verbatim_quote: These metrics measure the average deviation of the model's predicted probability vector from the one-hot encoded ground truth label

symbol_and_unit_ledger.p_hat_i: predicted softmax probability vector for sample i [dimensionless, simplex]

assumptions: RMSE computed on softmax probability vectors against one-hot labels.
Reported RMSE 0.1205; interpreted as calibration/confidence deviation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: RMSE on probability vectors measures confidence alignment, not class correctness; a confident wrong prediction still incurs large deviation.

layer2.mapping: Probability-vector RMSE IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSE calibration-uncertainty scoring: deviation of the full predictive distribution from truth is the Foundry's continuous calibration signal, distinct from discrete hit/miss grading.
layer2.telemetry: RMSE 0.1205; softmax vs one-hot; Euclidean norm; calibration deviation.

primitives.name: MAE of predicted probability vector vs one-hot truth
primitives.verbatim_quote: To quantify prediction deviation, we computed the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of the predicted probability distributions.
assumptions: MAE computed on softmax probability vectors against one-hot labels.
Reported MAE 0.0156 for ViSK-GAT.
primitives.breakdown_regime: L1 deviation is less sensitive to large single-class errors than RMSE; both measure distribution alignment rather than argmax correctness.

layer2.mapping: Probability-vector MAE IS a DERIVED KERNEL for GSE robust calibration scoring: the L1 companion to RMSE gives the Foundry a less outlier-sensitive view of how far the predictive distribution sits from truth.
layer2.telemetry: MAE 0.0156; softmax vs one-hot; L1 norm.

primitives.name: Friedman non-parametric test for backbone ranking significance
primitives.verbatim_quote: The test ranks each model across multiple evaluation conditions and assesses whether the ranking pattern is consistent.

symbol_and_unit_ledger.R_j: mean rank of model j across conditions [rank]

assumptions: Baseline M1 concat-only F1 0.8712; +ResB M2 +3.16%; +FGAM M3 +5.01%; +MGCM M4 +6.73%.

reasoning_traces.think:
ViSK-GAT, the Visual-Skeletal Geometric Attention Transformer of Rahman and colleagues (arXiv 2509.05913v3), is a multimodal deep learning framework that classifies musculoskeletal risk in athletes from a single monocular image paired with its 2D skeleton. The sovereign core is a disciplined observation pipeline: MediaPipe emits 33 anatomical landmarks as normalized coordinates with a visibility confidence, landmarks below 0.5 confidence are dropped, and joint angles are recovered by the cosine law on keypoint triplets while trunk inclination uses an epsilon-guarded arctangent that explicitly names its near-vertical division-by-zero breakdown. These angles feed a rule-based Rapid Entire Body Assessment implementation in which trunk, neck, and leg scores compose Group A, upper arm, lower arm, and wrist compose Group B, and a predefined Group C matrix maps the pair to one of eight ordinal risk classes. Crucially the model learns to predict the output of this fixed ergonomic function rather than an unconstrained mapping, and because the data are single-frame static images the load and activity modifiers are fixed to zero. That single decision is the paper's most important epistemic boundary: it declares, in advance, the causal modifiers it cannot observe.

The architectural contribution is a two-stage attention pipeline that refuses to treat fusion as a single undivided operation. The Fine-Grained Attention Module first refines the image modality against itself, using eight-head self-attention and two lightweight Transformer blocks with a 128-to-512-to-128 feed-forward expansion, so that cross-modal alignment later operates on posture-cue-aware features rather than diffuse general-purpose activations. The Multimodal Geometric Correspondence Module then performs an explicitly asymmetric cross-attention: image tokens are queries while skeletal coordinate tokens are both keys and values, a choice motivated by the biomechanical reality that joint positions should guide the selection of relevant visual features. Both modalities are projected into a shared 256-dimensional latent space, the attention output is concatenated with the image feature, and two stacked four-head Transformer layers plus a linear-LayerNorm-GELU fusion head produce a 512-dimensional joint embedding for classification. The ablation ladder quantifies why each stage matters: concatenation alone scores 0.8712 F1, residual blocks add 3.16 points, FGAM adds 5.01, and MGCM adds 6.73, while replacing cross-attention with concatenation inside MGCM costs 2.82 points, the largest single drop, proving that geometric alignment cannot be recovered by stacking features.

The evaluation is unusually thorough for a compact model and is the reason this paper is a strong Foundry citizen. The MusDis-Sports dataset comprises 8989 annotated image-skeleton-class triples compiled from four public sports datasets, with labeling reliability audited by an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.84 across varied viewing scales and a manual sanity check on 500 random images. The full model reaches 93.89 percent test accuracy, 93.85 percent F1, Cohen's Kappa 0.93, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient 0.93, with probability-vector RMSE 0.1205 and MAE 0.0156, and a Friedman rank test across four evaluation conditions returns p equal to 1.87 times ten to the minus five, confirming the backbone differences are statistically significant rather than noise. The metric suite itself is sovereign: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, MCC, Kappa, RMSE, and MAE are each printed as exact equations, and the authors explicitly warn that accuracy alone misleads under imbalance, which is why they lean on the chance-adjusted Kappa and MCC. A controlled fusion ladder shows early fusion at 71.31 percent, late fusion at 84.23, standard cross-attention at 88.77, and the full FGAM-plus-MGCM stack at 93.89, all under identical data and hyperparameters.

The failure analysis is where the paper earns its breakdown-regime discipline and where the Foundry extracts its most reusable vetoes. Performance is not uniform: the extreme-risk classes 7 and 8 are classified with exceptional reliability, false-negative rates of 0.0121 and 0.0051 and specificity above 0.99, which the authors correctly identify as the most critical requirement in a risk system. The moderate-risk boundary classes 2 and 4 are the weak points, because the angular thresholds separating them from adjacent classes are narrow, so a small estimation error in any single joint shifts the predicted label to a neighbor; class 2 carries the highest false-discovery rate of 0.1154 and class 4 the highest false-negative rate of 0.1565. The physical causes are named honestly: severe self-occlusion, motion blur, loose garments, and non-standard viewpoints compress depth in the 2D projection and distort estimated joint angles, with the climber pressed against a near-vertical rock surface as the canonical class-4 failure. These are not generic caveats but localized, mechanism-linked breakdown regimes, exactly the form the Foundry requires every sovereign operator to carry.

Implementation invariants and deployment evidence complete the picture. The selected recipe is AdamW with weight decay 1e-5, a OneCycleLR schedule peaking at 3e-4 with ten percent warmup and a decay factor of 1000, batch size 16, 100 epochs, 224-by-224 images, categorical cross-entropy with 0.1 label smoothing and gradient clipping at 1.0, on a 70/10/20 split; depth ablations show two Transformer blocks are optimal in both FGAM and MGCM and a third overfits the compact 512-dimensional fused representation. The whole model is only 5.8 million parameters, 22.8 megabytes trainable, and runs at 8.2 milliseconds per frame, 122 frames per second, on an RTX 3060, so it is genuinely deployable for real-time monitoring. The declared limitations are the final sovereign boundary: the 2D approximation introduces known variation versus 3D biomechanics, external load and repetitive activity cannot be reliably estimated from visual data alone, and the model is therefore most directly applicable where risk is predominantly postural. For GSI this is a clean isomorphism of the Foundry's own doctrine, a dimensioned, breakdown-aware, scope-declared operator whose every claim is tied to a printed equation, a measured reliability statistic, or a named failure mechanism, with zero sportsbook content and zero fabricated mathematics.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage runs from occupational ergonomics to athletic computer vision. Hignett and McAtamney's Rapid Entire Body Assessment (Applied Ergonomics 2000) supplied the ordinal Group A/B/C lookup structure; McAtamney and Corlett's RULA and the OWAS and OCRA protocols are the sibling assessment traditions the paper surveys. The vision branch descends from Li et al.'s CNN-to-2D-posture RULA pipeline, Kim et al.'s OpenPose 3D semi-automatic RULA/REBA, and Seo et al.'s OWAS construction-posture classifier, then through MediaPipe-based markerless frameworks such as Habeeba et al.'s FusionPose cyclist injury-risk model. The multimodal branch inherits Xiahou et al.'s sensor feature-level fusion, Zhang et al.'s infrared-plus-pressure cross-modal self-attention, and Narayan et al.'s compact convolutional transformer. ViSK-GAT's novel retrocausal step is to refuse single-block fusion: it inserts intra-modal FGAM refinement before an asymmetric, biomechanically grounded MGCM cross-attention, and it labels with a rule-based REBA function so the network predicts a transparent target rather than an opaque one. The 2D approximation and zeroed load/activity modifiers are deliberate scope choices inherited from the monocular-data constraint, not oversights.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The authors reason about three audiences at once. For the ergonomics community they preserve REBA's interpretable Group A/B/C structure and report ICC 0.84 plus a 500-image manual sanity check, anticipating the objection that automatically derived labels are untrustworthy. For the deep learning community they run a controlled backbone ladder, a Friedman significance test, and stepwise plus intra-module ablations, anticipating the objection that a novel architecture is just a bigger black box; they answer with a 5.8M-parameter model that beats 85M-parameter ViT and BEiT backbones. For the deployment engineer they report 8.2ms-per-frame inference and a 22.8MB footprint, anticipating the objection that accuracy is useless if it cannot run in real time. Most tellingly they model the safety auditor's mind by foregrounding high-risk-class reliability and by naming, class by class, the exact occlusion and threshold-proximity mechanisms that cause the moderate-risk failures, rather than hiding behind an aggregate accuracy. The zeroed load/activity modifiers show they also model the reviewer who will ask whether the score covers load-driven risk, and they concede the boundary explicitly.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The Foundry adjudicates this paper across its layers with several vetoes. The observation layer passes because every primitive is dimensioned and carries a breakdown regime: the cosine-law angle names its zero-norm singularity, the trunk arctangent names its epsilon guard and horizontal divergence, and the visibility filter names its hard 0.5 cutoff. The labeling layer passes the provenance gate because the target is a fixed rule-based REBA function with measured ICC reliability, not an unconstrained mapping. The fusion layer issues a positive veto against concatenation: the B1 ablation proves geometric alignment cannot be recovered by stacking, so any GSE kernel that fuses modalities by naive concatenation when spatial correspondence is the task is rejected. The capacity layer vetoes depth beyond two Transformer blocks on ablation evidence. The scope layer issues the strongest veto: because load and activity modifiers are zeroed and 2D projection distorts under occlusion, the operator is certified only for predominantly-postural, well-observed risk and must never be silently promoted to full load-and-repetition assessment. The safety layer prioritizes high-risk-class recall, matching the Foundry rule that certification weight follows the cost of the error. Zero sportsbook lines appear anywhere; the paper is pure physical-reasoning and clinical-telemetry territory.

universal_lens: ViSK-GAT is a universal observation-to-decision template: a dimensioned, visibility-gated body-state observation is lifted into a latent space, refined within each modality, aligned across modalities by an asymmetric geometric correspondence, and read by a calibrated ordinal-risk head whose every claim is bounded by a named breakdown regime and a declared scope of observability. The pattern generalizes to any sovereign system that must turn noisy physical telemetry into an auditable, safety-weighted decision.
gsi_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Institute this is a direct bioenergetic and clinical-telemetry kernel: cosine-law joint angles and epsilon-guarded trunk inclination become joint-stress primitives, the REBA Group A/B/C composition becomes an interpretable regional-load aggregator, and the visibility filter plus ICC label audit become the provenance gate for athlete posture monitoring. The high-risk-class reliability priority maps to GSI's injury-prevention mandate, while the zeroed load/activity modifiers and 2D occlusion breakdown define exactly where a monocular posture model must defer to instrumented 3D biomechanics.
gse_mapping: For Galaxy Sports Edge the paper supplies reusable decision kernels: asymmetric geometric cross-attention is the fusion operator that grounds an appearance prior in a sovereign physical state, the concatenation-insufficiency ablation is a fusion-necessity veto, the depth-overfit ablation is a capacity-budget veto, the Friedman test is a ranking-significance gate, and the probability-vector RMSE/MAE are continuous calibration signals. The boundary-proximity and occlusion failure regimes become GSE uncertainty vetoes that flag narrow-threshold and poorly-observed states rather than emitting a confident hard label, and the postural-only scope declaration is the domain-of-validity gate the Foundry enforces on every operator.
